approach: Systematic case analysis: even n (trivial), odd n mod 4 = 3 (greedy), odd n mod 4 = 1 (hard)
findings: Proved for all even n (x=n/2,y=n,z=n). Proved for n≡3(mod 4) via greedy (x=(n+1)/4). Hard case: n≡1(mod 4), especially primes p≡1(mod 4). The 6 hard residue classes mod 840 are all in this category. Next approach: focus on algebraic identity construction for primes p≡1(mod 4), specifically the decomposition of 12/(p(p+3)) into 2 unit fractions.
